gloss: to become familiar with; to fit in; to blend in

definitions.gloss: to become familiar with; to get used to
definitions.explanation: To gradually become accustomed to a new environment, person, or situation over time.

definitions.gloss: to fit in; to blend in; to suit
definitions.explanation: For something to harmonize well with its surroundings, or for a quality or concept to be compatible with something.

examples.japanese: この{土地|とち}にすっかり{馴染|なじ}んだ。
examples.english: I've completely gotten used to this area.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{職場|しょくば}に{馴染|なじ}むのに{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to get used to the new workplace.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちはすぐに{新|あたら}しい{先生|せんせい}に{馴染|なじ}んだ。
examples.english: The children quickly warmed up to the new teacher.

examples.japanese: この{色|いろ}は{部屋|へや}に{馴染|なじ}む。
examples.english: This color blends in with the room.

examples.japanese: {革|かわ}のかばんは{使|つか}ううちに{手|て}に{馴染|なじ}んでくる。
examples.english: A leather bag gradually molds to your hand as you use it.

examples.japanese: この{提案|ていあん}は{日本|にほん}の{商|しょう}習慣に{馴染|なじ}まない。
examples.english: This proposal doesn't fit with Japanese business customs.

notes:
{馴染|なじ}む is an intransitive godan verb.

ASPECT (ている):
{馴染|なじ}んでいる describes the resulting state of being accustomed or fitting in well.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [place/person]に{馴染|なじ}む — to get used to; to blend into
- [noun]に{馴染|なじ}まない — to not suit; to be incompatible with

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土地|とち}に{馴染|なじ}む (get used to a place)
- {手|て}に{馴染|なじ}む (fit the hand, feel natural in hand)
- {肌|はだ}に{馴染|なじ}む (suit the skin)

Often written in kana as なじむ. The related noun {馴染|なじ}み means "familiarity" or "a regular (customer)." The expression {顔馴染|かおなじ}み means "familiar face" or "acquaintance."
